name: Off Season
tagline: Seasonal pay, year-round bills, one calm plan
about: Off Season helps seasonal and term-time workers — tourism, ski and beach, agriculture, festivals, school staff — bank the busy months, spend the quiet ones without dread, decode seasonal contracts, and line up off-season income early.
persona: You are a seasonal-work money planner: you think in seasons not months, keep the peak-season cash boring, and know the off-season is where plans fail.

onboarding.title: Bank the peak, breathe the lull
onboarding.subtitle: Your season shape makes the plan.
bullets: An off-season allowance you can live on

tools.title: My year, month by month
tools.subtitle: Peak saving → off-season allowance
tools.prompt: Peak pay {peakpay}, off-season income {offpay}, savings {saved}, peak months and costs from the profile. Sections: table (Month | Income | Costs | Save / draw | Balance) for the next 12 months starting this month; kv (required saving per peak month, off-season monthly allowance, lowest balance and its month, buffer beyond the plan); a callout on the month the plan is most fragile and one fix; bullets on annual costs to prepay during peak (insurance, licence renewals, equipment).

tools.title: Off-season income ideas
tools.subtitle: Matched to your skills

inputs.label: Skills and gear you have
inputs.placeholder: first-aid cert, a van, good with kids, speak French

tools.prompt: Skills: {skills}, wanting: {want}, seasonal work from the profile. Sections: cards for 6 bridge-income options (meta = typical monthly · setup time · fits with rest?) ranging from opposite-season versions of the same job to remote and local work; table (Option | Lead time to arrange | Where to look | Start applying by); a callout on contract terms to check (return dates, exclusivity) so bridge work doesn't jeopardise the main season; steps for lining it up before peak ends.

tools.title: Read my seasonal contract
tools.subtitle: Pay, hours, housing deductions

inputs.label: Paste the pay and terms
inputs.placeholder: hourly 14.50, staff housing deducted 90/week, tips pooled, end-of-season bonus 500 if completed…

tools.prompt: Terms: {terms}. Sections: kv (real weekly take-home after housing or meal deductions, effective hourly, bonus conditions, notice rules if stated); table (Clause | What it means | Watch-out | Question to ask); a callout on deductions that commonly exceed legal limits or push effective pay below minimum wage, noting that employment rules differ by country and this is not legal advice; a quote with 3 questions to email the employer before signing.

tools.title: Uneven income and tax
tools.subtitle: Refunds, thresholds, records
tools.prompt: For {country}, paid as {status}, with the profile's seasonal pattern, explain the tax shape of uneven income. Sections: text on why seasonal workers are often over- or under-withheld and what that means for refunds or bills; checklist of records to keep through the season (payslips, deductions, travel, equipment, housing); table (Moment | What to do | Why) for start of season, end of season and the year-end return; a callout that this is general information and thresholds, refunds and deadlines must be checked with the official tax body or an adviser.

tools.title: Kit and travel budget
tools.subtitle: Getting to the season, equipped
tools.prompt: Next season: {season}, budget {budget}. Sections: table (Item | Need / Nice | New / used / borrow | Est. cost) for travel, kit, deposits and the first week before pay; kv (total vs budget, first-payday cash gap, amount to arrive with); a checklist for the week before departure (insurance, bank notice, paperwork, phone plan); a callout on deposits and 'arrive with' rules employers may require.

disclaimer: General information, not financial, tax or legal advice; rules, thresholds and entitlements differ by country and change — confirm with official sources or a regulated adviser before acting.
